title: Olmec civilization
summary: From about 1200 to 400 BCE the Olmec of the Gulf Coast lowlands of Veracruz and Tabasco built the first complex culture in Mesoamerica with monumental art and architecture. San Lorenzo, the earliest centre, flourished until about 900 BCE, when La Venta took its place and raised one of the largest pyramids of its day. Olmec carvers set colossal basalt portrait heads of rulers in their cities. Their gods, ritual, ball courts and planned ceremonial precincts shaped every later Mesoamerican civilization.

uncertainty.note: Standard archaeological dating for the Early and Middle Formative Olmec horizon spans c. 1200 BCE (astronomical -1199) to c. 400 BCE (astronomical -399).

where.modern_name: San Lorenzo Tenochtitlán, southern Veracruz, Mexico (representative center of the Olmec heartland)
where.historical_name: San Lorenzo and the Olmec heartland, Gulf Coast lowlands of Mesoamerica

importance.justification: The first complex Mesoamerican culture, whose religion, art and city plans shaped later civilizations there (R3 D2 T4 L3).
